directions.name: Signal Chain
directions.oneLiner: His site is an oscilloscope that locks onto a full stack developer: one noisy signal snaps into four clean layers and their sum, and every system he has shipped sits on the bench, wired as built, for you to probe.
directions.concept: Prajwal trained in Electronics & Communication (BE, KVGCE Sullia, 2021-2025) and now ships production systems end to end as a Full Stack Developer at Maruti Flex Traders LLP. His own sentence, 'turning ideas into complete applications, from designing responsive frontend interfaces and developing backend APIs to integrating databases, implementing business logic, deploying applications', is a signal chain: messy input, conditioned through stages, a working output. So the portfolio is the instrument he was trained on. It opens untriggered: one noisy trace standing for the operations his projects start from (a TVS showroom, telecallers, venue bookings, DGCA drone rules, MRI screening). The trigger catches and the noise resolves into four labelled channels (Interface, Services, Data, Intelligence) plus Σ, the shipped system that is literally their sum. Further down, every system sits on a bench as a board generated from its own repository: chips are its components, copper is its connections, and you clip probes on to see the shape of its traffic and flip its one honest what-if. Case studies are datasheets; the career is a revision table. The ECE degree stops being a footnote and becomes the proof that he thinks in whole systems, from ESP32 firmware on a traffic pole to a RAG pipeline behind FastAPI.
directions.signatureMoment: THE LOCK, then THE PROBE. A dark graticule with one noisy, untriggered trace rolling across it; the status reads AUTO. The trigger catches: AUTO flips to TRIG'D, the noise collapses with a 2% overshoot, and the single messy signal splits into five clean lanes: 1 Interface, 2 Services, 3 Data, 4 Intelligence and Σ Shipped system, which is literally their sum. Above them PRAJWAL M P resolves by sample-and-hold in five hard steps. Anyone can then drag the bone T handle off the signal: the whole stack loses lock and rolls back into noise, and re-locks 1.2s after release. The sentence people repeat is 'his site turns noise into a full stack'. Four screens later the metaphor pays off with evidence: on the bench, clip a probe onto the Drone Intelligence System's /ws/kpi connection and the scope shows its push bursts; press 'Gemini unavailable' and the request visibly re-routes through the fallback path his README documents. It sticks because it is his job: turning messy real operations into layered systems that keep working. (The Lock is built and verified in the working prototype; the bench is this refinement.)

directions.layoutSystem:
An oscilloscope graticule: a 10-division column grid (4 on portrait) inside margins of clamp(16px,4vw,64px). The WebGL graticule is drawn from the same rect, so DOM type and canvas lines align. 8px base (8/16/24/40/64/104); section padding 16-24vh, so each screen breathes like an instrument display.
Two materials:
- SCREENS (graphite) carry live signals: hero, statement, bench, contact.
- SHEETS (bone) carry records: history and the /work datasheets. The material change itself marks the move from signal to record. Datasheets follow TI structure: a 220px label column (section number + mono label) beside the content column.
Rules:
1. Headlines, nav and body are plain language (Work, Stack, Experience, Contact). Instrument dialect lives only in 10-11px mono labels.
2. Every number is set in mono.
3. Colour is functional only: four channel colours encode the same four layers everywhere (hero lanes, chip outlines on the bench, BOM groups, datasheet labels); bone is Σ and 'you'. No orange, no glow beyond the beam itself, no cards, no glass.
4. Measured asymmetry: big type left-aligned to division lines, labels pinned to edges like bezel engraving, generous negative space.
Persistent chrome: a fixed top bar with P.M.P / Full Stack Developer, the record-view nav (a miniature 'scope record' of the whole page with section ticks and a sliding viewport bracket), the TRIG'D indicator, Résumé and Contact. Tailwind CSS v4 carries the tokens (palette, spacing, division sizes) as CSS variables shared with the shaders.
directions.openingSequence:
First visit, about 3.0s, played over the real hero DOM (an intro, not a loader).
- 0-150ms: the beam spot powers on at the left edge (opacity, power2.out) with a phosphor bloom.
- 150-1050ms: the beam sweeps left to right (cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1)) drawing the raw composite (the sum of the four channel waveforms plus noise) with 75ms persistence; graticule lines materialise 140px behind it.
- 1050-1450ms: free-run. The trace rolls at 0.32 screen-widths/s; the status blinks AUTO at 2Hz.
- 1450ms: trigger. TRIG'D; the roll stops in 180ms (power2.out); phases snap; noise falls to 0.6% over 500ms on the 'lock' CustomEase (M0,0 C.14,.62 .2,1.04 .34,1.02 .5,.99 .64,1 1,1: a 2% overshoot, then settle).
- 1500-2100ms: split. The composite separates into CH1-CH4 + Σ; lanes travel to their rows (lock ease); colour fades from bone into the channel colours.
- 1720-2570ms: the name resolves by sample-and-hold in five hard steps of 170ms (steps, not tweens: sampling is discrete). The h1 is painted from frame 0 through the mask, so LCP is not delayed.
- 2100-2800ms: 'Full Stack Developer' beam-wipes in (clip-path, 700ms, cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1)) with a 1.5px bone beam riding the edge.
- 2450-3000ms: the chrome (kicker, lede, CTA row, lane chips, NOW line, trigger handle, scroll cue) fades and slides 10px, 35ms stagger, 500ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1).
Skip: any key, pointerdown, wheel or touch sets timeScale(9) and the sequence finishes in about 0.3s; scroll is never blocked.
Repeat visit in the same session (sessionStorage): the same timeline at timeScale 2.6, about 1.15s. Returning from a datasheet: no intro. Reduced motion: a single locked frame.
Failsafe: an inline head script unhides everything at 5.2s; without JS everything is visible from the start. No sound, ever. Once the lock settles the hero loop stops (zero idle draws) until the pointer or trigger wakes it.

directions.interactiveBackground:
One raw WebGL2 canvas fills the hero, deliberately not three.js, so the critical path stays at about 6KB gz.
Rendering:
- Each channel is instanced beam segments (720 per channel desktop, 360 mobile); waveforms are evaluated in the vertex shader from uniforms, so the CPU does no per-frame geometry work.
- The fragment shader uses woscope's analytic Gaussian-beam integral (two erf calls), so steep edges render dimmer like a real CRT.
- Additive accumulation into a half-float ping-pong FBO decaying with τ = 75ms gives frame-rate-independent persistence; a composite pass draws the graticule procedurally (10x8 landscape, 4x10 portrait) and tone-maps 1-e^(-1.7x). Bloom is capped so traces read as phosphor, not neon.
Shapes are a visual code for each layer, and the legend says so: Interface = smooth sine (continuous UI), Services = square request/response, Data = staircase write ramp, Intelligence = AM-modulated carrier, Σ = their sum.
Pointer (the probe, fine pointers only): the nearest lane brightens 1.75x and the others drop to 0.45x; that lane's chip expands to list the real technologies on the layer; a bone dashed measurement cursor follows the pointer's x; traces under the probe ripple slightly (a Gaussian-windowed damped sine whose energy comes from pointer speed and decays as e^(-2.6t)).
Trigger: the bone T handle on the Σ lane is a role=slider (drag and arrow keys). Moving it more than 0.85 amplitude off the signal loses lock: channels roll at four speeds, noise rises, status AUTO. It re-locks 1.2s after release with the lock ease.
Render discipline (architect judge fix): converge-then-stop. Once lock energy falls below 1e-3 the loop halts at 0 draws; pointer, trigger or resize wake it. Paused off-screen (IntersectionObserver) and on hidden tabs. Uniforms come from a layout cache, never from per-frame getComputedStyle.
Touch: no hover and no idle animation: a still, locked picture. Lane chips are tap toggles; the trigger supports touch-drag (touch-action: none on the handle only).
Adaptive quality: if the 90-frame median exceeds 20ms, drop to DPR 1 and half the segments; above 24ms, freeze to a static frame.

directions.threeD:
Exactly one 3D element: the Bench board, a single-layer circuit board generated per system from data/systems.ts. There is no layer stack anywhere in this direction: the prototype's five-layer PCB stackup is retired because the judges noted four concepts converged on exploded stacks, and Through-Line owns that image.
Build: an R3F chunk (next/dynamic, ssr:false) imported when Systems is within 1.2 viewports and prefetched on idle after LCP on desktop. A graphite FR4 board with bone silkscreen; chips are low rounded boxes in five columns (CH1-CH4 + Σ) with channel-colour outlines; labels are baked into one CanvasTexture per system (redrawn once per acquisition, never per frame); connections are one merged Line2 batch with constant pixel width; four probe hooks are tube curves with clips in the channel colours. An orthographic 3/4 camera (35° tilt) with damped pointer tilt of ±4° (600ms); DOM labels for the active chip are projected after updateMatrixWorld, so they stay crisp, selectable and translatable.
Why it earns its place: it is the real architecture from his repository, and clipping a probe onto a connection completes the instrument metaphor: you measure his work instead of reading claims about it.
Interaction: hover or tap a connection to probe it (the clip re-seats in 300ms and the scope shows that connection on CH1); hover or tap a chip for its role and technology; the what-if control re-routes the path; a bone request pulse travels the copper at constant speed, because signals don't ease. Motion (LazyMotion) handles the React-state UI around it: probe readout swaps, what-if states, copy feedback.
Performance: frameloop='demand'; ≤30 draw calls and under 5k triangles; DPR clamp 1.75 desktop / 1.25 tablet; probe and what-if changes only update uniforms; a pending-selection queue applies picks made before the scene is ready (a race already fixed in the prototype).
Degradation: phones and portrait tablets get the SVG board; no WebGL2, deviceMemory ≤2 or Save-Data → SVG; reduced motion → a static board, instant probe swaps and no pulses.
The hero stays 2D on purpose: a scope is a 2D instrument.

directions.name: Cross-Section
directions.oneLiner: One instrument, a blue metrology laser, cuts through his name, through every system he has shipped and through the real ground he comes from, to show what is inside: solid all the way through.
directions.concept: One instrument, used everywhere: a section plane, drawn as a single blue laser line like the ones metrology scanners sweep across a part. It cuts things open to show what they are made of, and it comes from Prajwal's record. His first-place final-year project trained a CNN on 12,000+ MRI images, which are slices, to find what was hidden inside. He was schooled in Koppa, in the Malnad hills, ground that maps describe with contour lines, which are sections too. And 'Full Stack Developer' is a claim you can only check by cutting through: interface, logic, data, AI, delivery. So the hero is a specimen: his name, sectioned, plaster surface above and dark interior below. Scroll and each system's surface (what users do) is cut away to its interior (how it is wired, drawn from its own repository). The faint contours behind the surface are real SRTM elevation data for the ground between Koppa, Sullia and Bengaluru; in the Experience chapter they stand up into a plaster relief sliced along his actual route. One palette (plaster, ink, interior black, one laser blue), one gesture, one claim. Layers never separate in depth: the only move is a planar cut.
directions.signatureMoment: THE SCAN. Each system arrives as a specimen showing its surface: a plain user story ('Ask India's drone rules in plain language, check compliance, work out flight time and ROI.') and, where one exists, a real capture of the live product. As you scroll, a 2px laser line travels down the panel 1:1 with the wheel, no easing, no snapping. Everything above the line is cut away to the dark interior, which holds the system's wiring drawn from its repository: React 19 dashboard → FastAPI → ChromaDB (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, top 5) → Gemini 2.0 Flash, with the MCP server docked beside it and Docker underneath. A mono label riding the blade reads 'Cutting · Data', each block lights the instant the blade crosses it, and when the section completes one request pulse runs through the wiring at constant speed. Scroll back and the surface heals. The first cut is his own name: on arrival the hero is already a specimen, PRAJWAL M P sectioned with its lower third bone on black. People retell it as 'his site cuts every project open and you see exactly how it is wired inside'. The closing twist: the contour lines behind every page turn out to be the real hills around Koppa, and in Experience they stand up into a plaster relief sliced along Koppa → Sullia → Bengaluru. (The scan, cut glyphs, relief and profile are verified in the prototype; the wiring interiors, the sectioned hero and the blue laser are this refinement.)

directions.openingSequence:
Total 2.4s, skippable and LCP-safe: the h1 is painted in Ink at first paint and only its surroundings animate.
- Beat 1 (0-300ms): on plaster, a 1px Laser Blue line draws from the centre outward at the top edge (scaleX 0→1, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)).
- Beat 2 (300-1300ms): the line sweeps top to bottom in 1.0s on cubic-bezier(.37,0,.63,1), near-constant like a scanner bed. Above it the real-terrain contours resolve (shader uReveal with a 2.5% soft edge); as it crosses the name, each glyph's cross-section flashes blue in a 3.5px band.
- Beat 3 (1300-1900ms): the plane rises back to rest at 66% of the name's cap height (600ms, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)) and cuts: below it the lower third of PRAJWAL M P turns Bone on Interior, and the lower 55% of the viewport opens into the interior (a mask from the bottom edge up to the plane, same 600ms).
- Beat 4 (1550-2250ms): in the interior, 'Full Stack Developer', the statement, 'Now: Maruti Flex Traders LLP' and 'Based in Bengaluru' rise out of masks (yPercent 115→0, 750ms, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), 80ms stagger); the readout 'CUT 790 m · KOPPA' fades in at the right end of the line. The hiring message is legible by about 2.0s.
- Beat 5 (1800-2400ms): five slice-plan nav lines draw left to right (550ms, 70ms stagger); the HUD fades in.
Skip: the first wheel, key, touch or pointerdown jumps to the identical end state with no flash.
Repeat visit in the session: 2.6x speed (about 0.95s). Returning from a case page: no intro. Reduced motion: the final state at first paint.
If WebGL is late, a pre-rendered contour poster (AVIF, same projection) is revealed by the same sweep.
directions.heroTypography:
'PRAJWAL M P' in Mona Sans 850 / wdth 100, fitted across 12 columns, built from three stacked layers:
1. The real h1 in Ink, clipped to everything above the plane.
2. An aria-hidden copy in Bone on the Interior, clipped below the plane.
3. An aria-hidden Laser Blue copy clipped to a 3.5px band at the plane: where the laser crosses a letter you see that letter's exact cross-section in blue; between letters the laser is a 62%-opacity hairline.
At rest the plane sits at 66% of the cap height, so the name is visibly a specimen (top two-thirds ink on plaster, bottom third bone on black). Because the whole region below changes material, it reads as cut open, not crossed out (the recruiter judge's 'strikethrough' fix), and a blue line carries no 'deleted' or 'error' connotation.
Pointer Y (fine pointers) moves the plane inside the name band only (cap line to 40px below the baseline; lerp 0.14 per 60fps frame), and the same value sets the elevation cut through the land behind (1,700 m at the cap line to 60 m at the bottom of the band); the readout reports it ('CUT 1,060 m · GHATS').
Horizontal pointer velocity shears the two halves apart along the cut (an impulse of 9 × movementX into a spring with k=190 and c=17, clamped to ±11px, settling in about 0.5s), only while the plane is inside the letters, so it reads as slicing a solid and never as a glitch.
'Full Stack Developer' (Mona Sans 700) sits directly beneath in Bone, the first thing read after the name. Touch: no shear; a tap sets the cut for 2.8s, then it eases back to rest; nothing moves while idle (the prototype's perpetual breathing is removed).
directions.interactiveBackground:
Real ground as a contour plan. Technically: one fixed raw WebGL2 canvas (about 5KB; three.js stays off the critical path) running one fragment shader over a heightmap of SRTM/GMTED elevation for 74.95-77.95°E × 12.22-13.91°N, the region holding Koppa, Sullia and Bengaluru, baked at build time to a 512×296 16-bit R/G PNG (about 140KB, fetched after LCP at low priority).
- Lines every 100 m at 5% ink and index lines every 500 m at 10%, anti-aliased with fwidth and faded on steep slopes; a ±4% north-west hillshade gives the plaster its material.
- The pointer's cut elevation draws ONE contour in Laser Blue with a soft halo, plus a faint 45° section hatch (the drafting convention for cut material) over all land higher than the cut, so moving the plane visibly floods and drains the real landscape. Every other line stays neutral; this replaces the prototype's scattered red and pink iso-lines, which the judges found busy.
- Quiet zones: up to six DOM text rects (vec4 uniforms) drop lines to 25% and the hatch to 0 behind copy.
Scroll: no per-pixel coupling. On each chapter entry the view eases for 1.2s to the next waypoint along Koppa → Sullia (widening 300 → 420 units) and renders only during that tween. The canvas stops under interior sections (IntersectionObserver) and on hidden tabs.
Render discipline: on demand only (pointer, resize, tween), zero idle draws, layout rects cached by ResizeObserver and never read per frame.
Touch: a tap sets the cut for 2.8s; no idle animation.
Fallbacks: a contour poster AVIF (about 60KB) for no WebGL2, Save-Data or deviceMemory ≤2; reduced motion renders once at 790 m; prefers-contrast: more drops the contours to flat plaster.

directions.name: Through-Line
directions.oneLiner: A short film on warm paper in which one red thread runs from Prajwal's name through every layer each system really uses, knotting where it is built and passing empty where it is not.
directions.concept: In screenwriting the through-line is the thread that connects every scene; in German it is der rote Faden, the red thread. In Prajwal's work it is literal. His own GitHub sentence, 'from designing responsive frontend interfaces and developing backend APIs to integrating databases, implementing business logic, deploying applications', describes one person carrying one idea from interface to production. So the site has exactly one colour: a 2px laterite-red thread that never breaks. It underlines his name on the title card, binds the five layers beside it, drops into a stack of five paper plates where it sews through each system he built, leads the cuts between his selected work, strings Koppa, Sullia and Bengaluru together, and finally underlines his email. The film lives in the motion, not the costume: a title card that lights up, cuts, a focus pull, a fade to black. Projects are told with real artifacts (the RAG path from the Drone README, the Audify pipeline, a live BookMyVenue capture), never mockups, and in his own first-person voice. His pattern repeats across them: messy operations (a TVS showroom, telecallers, venue bookings, DGCA drone rules, MRI screening) become complete systems.
directions.signatureMoment: THE THREADING. The title's red rule turns a corner, drops off the hero and, through a focus pull, lands in a paper studio where five plates hang exploded: 01 Interface, 02 Logic, 03 Data, 04 Intelligence, 05 Delivery. Pick a system and the thread needles down through the stack in 1.4s (power2.inOut), tying a knot at every layer that system really uses and printing the real tool beside it. For the Drone Intelligence System: React 19 dashboard → FastAPI + WebSockets → ChromaDB vectors → Gemini 2.0 Flash RAG + MCP server → Docker Compose. A layer the system never touched gets an empty graphite grommet marked 'not part of this build': BookMyVenue's thread passes Intelligence untouched; Maruti Flex operations, his current job, passes it too and ends 'in production'. 'Full stack' becomes checkable, system by system, in one image. People retell it as 'you pick a project and a red thread sews through his whole stack, and skips the layers it did not use'. (The threading is built and verified in the prototype with three r187: five rounded-box plates, a TubeGeometry thread revealed by drawRange, DOM callouts.)

Objects:

BookMyVenue: React 18 + Vite → Express · JWT · bcrypt → JSON DB, no double booking → (grommet) → GitHub Actions → Pages. Smart Ambulance: Flutter → Express + Socket.IO → (grommet) → (grommet) → Mosquitto + ESP32 firmware, Docker.

Targets: LCP ≤1.8s on desktop and ≤2.5s on a mid-range Android over 4G; CLS ≤0.02; INP ≤150ms; Lighthouse mobile ≥90 performance and 100 accessibility; 60fps on desktop and ≥50fps on iPhone 12-class devices in Ch.01. Enforced in GitHub Actions with size-limit and Lighthouse CI budgets.

risks: Film devices tipping into kitsch. Rule: at most one film device per chapter; the film lives in motion (title card, cuts, focus pull, fade to black), not costume; the letterbox gate, animated grain, 'starring' billing and 'Filmed on location' are removed; copy is plain and first-person.

Without the terrain relief the hero background is quieter. The lit paper must be tuned on real devices: if it reads flat, raise the light pool's contrast, never the texture's; the thread and the letterpress carry the interaction.
Laterite can read as 'error'. It is reserved for the thread, the selects and focus; real errors use text plus an icon.

The Stack is the only layer stack across the three directions, but it can still be compared with Stripe Press's shelf or generic exploded stacks. It stays exploded, threaded, data-driven and lit like a paper studio, and the grommets are the point.
A 3D chapter immediately after the hero must never touch the LCP path: poster AVIF, idle prefetch, demand rendering, and no pin on phones.
Sofia Sans Extra Condensed's J descender crossing the thread may look like a collision at some sizes. Test at 320-2560px and fall back to placing the rule below the descender.
Livora overlap (ink, paper and lime with Bricolage, Inter and JetBrains Mono): warm paper, Laterite and Sofia Sans / Newsreader / DM Mono keep it distinct.
His current job has no public visuals, so its proof is a typographic one-sheet plus 'ask me about this work'; screenshots only with his employer's permission.

README provenance: the stills and threads use README details (Drone's all-MiniLM-L6-v2, top-5 retrieval, Gemini 2.0 Flash and four MCP tools; Audify's pipeline and Let's Encrypt; BookMyVenue's payment-time recheck and GitHub Actions deploy; Smart Ambulance topics), re-checked on 2026-11-05 against the fetched READMEs; Prajwal confirms them before launch. recommendation.reasoning: Pitch Signal Chain first. It is the only concept no judge ranked below second (7, 8 and 8), and it carries the strongest person-truth: the instrument he was trained on becomes the story of what he does now, so the moment people remember (noise locking into a full stack) is also the fastest read of his role. This refinement removes its two real weaknesses. First, the tech-count fingerprints are replaced by the bench: real architectures from his repositories that engineering leads can probe and stress with one honest what-if. That is Schematic's evidence, which two judges scored highest, grafted where it fits naturally, because a probe needs a scope. Second, the palette and the metaphor stack are disciplined: no orange, no PCB stackup, no test-point dots, plain-language navigation. It also has the most complete prototype (two static routes, working transitions, an LCP-safe intro, failsafes and a real motion toggle), so it is the lowest-risk path to an award-level build; validate it first with a 5-second recruiter test of the hero. Hold Cross-Section for a client who wants the most original, jury-facing piece: it was the Awwwards judge's first choice, it never needs a layer stack, and its sectioned name is the most iconic single image of the three. Hold Through-Line for a client who wants the warmest, calmest read and a human story: its threading is the most readable per-system proof in the set. Both are complete, buildable and stronger after these refinements.

whyTheseThree:
Exploded View was set aside: lowest scores, an echo of his own Livora hero, and a career-as-layers mapping that misfiled his current role. Schematic was the hardest cut. Two judges ranked it first, but it shared Signal Chain's world (dark and technical), type system (Archivo Expanded + Martian Mono) and vocabulary (BOM, J1, revisions), so keeping both would have given Prajwal two versions of the same answer. Its best ideas survive where they fit: per-system wiring drawn from his repositories with probes and one honest what-if (Signal Chain's bench, Cross-Section's interiors and case pages), constant-speed signals, a Signals pause toggle, zero-idle rendering and one data file behind diagrams and skills.

The three now differ on every axis the brief asked for:
- World: phosphor screens on graphite with bone record sheets / a plaster surface over a dark interior, whose hero is literally half light and half dark / warm cream paper that fades to black only at the end.
- 3D intensity: WebGL-forward (a custom erf-beam shader hero plus a 3D bench) / one shader background plus one real-terrain relief / a DOM-first hero with zero WebGL and a single paper scene.
- Type voice: expanded engineering grotesk + technical mono (Archivo, Martian Mono) / dense neutral grotesk + Swiss-lab mono (Mona Sans at normal width, Fragment Mono) / extra-condensed poster face + literary serif italic (Sofia Sans Extra Condensed, Newsreader, DM Mono). No two directions share a family.
- Storytelling device: acquire and probe / cut and section / thread and stitch.
- Accent: four functional phosphor channels with bone / one laser blue / one laterite red.

Collisions removed on purpose: the real terrain now belongs only to Cross-Section (Through-Line's hero is relit paper and its about is a one-screen triptych); the exploded layer stack belongs only to Through-Line (Signal Chain's PCB stackup became a single-layer bench, and Cross-Section never separates layers); Signal Chain's orange was removed and Cross-Section's red laser became blue, so the three heroes no longer all read as 'big name plus a red-orange line'.

On the request to dig into GitHub and LinkedIn: I re-checked every README-sourced detail used here against the READMEs fetched from github.com/Prajwalps2603. Confirmed: Drone's endpoints, local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, top-5 retrieval, Gemini 2.0 Flash, the HTTP 429 fallback and the four MCP tools; Smart Ambulance's MQTT topics and payloads (the README calls it a prototype); Audify's four speech-to-text providers, retry queue and Let's Encrypt HTTPS; BookMyVenue's payment-time recheck, simulated HMAC payment, 20 tests and GitHub Actions deploy. New flags from that check: ResumAI's README lists its OpenAI and PDF services as stubs, so no direction features it; Drone's live KPI stream uses simulated mission data and is labelled that way; the Brain Tumor README's front end is HTML/CSS/JS, so no direction claims React for it. The GitHub repo list also maps the unlinked dossier projects to real repos (CloudScape is AWS-Web-Hosting, Road Accident Detection is Vechile-Accident-System, plus Sudoku-Solver-DSA, Campus_Connect and LifeVault-AI), to be confirmed before linking. LinkedIn still returns HTTP 999 (an authwall) to automated requests, so nothing new came from it; any LinkedIn-only details would need to be pasted in by Prajwal.
